nodes.content: Build an incremental interprocedural alias analysis that preserves soundness across pointer escapes, indirect calls, and changing function summaries.
requirements: Soundly handle heap objects, pointer casts, recursion, and opaque external calls under documented IR semantics.
After single-function edits, match full recomputation’s alias answers while reducing median analysis latency by 50%.

nodes.content: Use allocation-site points-to constraints, cast-preserving propagation, indirect-call target expansion, conservative external escape summaries, and SCC-based summary invalidation.
How can changed escape summaries and indirect-call targets invalidate transitive callers without recomputing unaffected SCCs?
Versioned escape and call-target dependencies limit recomputation to impacted caller SCCs while preserving full-recompute alias answers.
Validate versioned SCC dependencies, implement conservative external summaries, then benchmark alias equivalence and median edit latency versus full recomputation.
Run EditSCC-200 single-function edit tests covering escapes, recursion, and indirect calls; compare invalidated SCCs and aliases against full recomputation.
EditSCC-200 found 3/200 alias mismatches: newly escaped global function pointers introduced callees absent from cached caller-SCC dependencies.
Adding global-escape watchers to versioned call-target dependencies will eliminate EditSCC-200 alias mismatches without recomputing unaffected SCCs.
Add global-escape watchers, rerun EditSCC-200 against full recomputation, and measure alias mismatches, invalidated SCCs, and median latency.
EditSCC-200: 0/200 alias mismatches; only dependency-reachable SCCs recomputed; median edit latency 42 ms versus 110 ms full.
Adopt global-escape watchers for SCC invalidation; EditSCC-200 resolves three prior mismatches and cuts median latency 62%.
Implement allocation-site heaps, conservative pointer casts, and opaque-call read/write/escape summaries; test recursive calls in IRSemantics-40.
Alias engine and IRSemantics-40 tests cover allocation-site heaps, conservative pointer casts, recursive SCC summaries, and opaque-call read/write/escape effects.
Which pointer-cast and opaque-call effects must recursive SCC summaries propagate to preserve sound allocation-site heap aliases?
Add grammar-generated IR edit fuzzing with full-recompute alias checks and latency gates for casts, opaque calls, and escaped function pointers.
Document cast and opaque-call semantics, build a full-recompute oracle, and baseline median latency on recursive single-function edits.
Extend IRSemantics-40 with cast round-trips, opaque-call escapes, and recursive heap edits; compare incremental aliases and timing against full recomputation.
IRSemantics-40 oracle suite records incremental/full alias diffs and edit latency for cast round-trips, opaque escapes, and recursive heap edits.
Run 10,000 grammar-generated single-function cast, escape, and recursion edits through IRSemantics-40; check oracle agreement and ≥50% median latency reduction.
Across 10,000 generated edits, alias mismatches were 0; median edit latency was 43 ms versus 112 ms full.
Adopt global-escape SCC invalidation and generated-edit CI gates; both benchmarks show zero mismatches and >50% median latency reductions.
Document pointer–integer cast provenance and opaque-call read/write/escape/return rules; test recursive SCC fixed points against IRSemantics-40.
IRSemantics-40 found two soundness failures in both modes: opaque-call returns could alias escaped heap objects but were modeled as fresh.
Which generated edit combinations exercise cast-induced escapes and indirect-call target changes together, beyond fixed regression cases?
Staged pointer-cast escapes, opaque-call returns, and indirect-call retargeting edits will expose may-alias omissions despite full-recompute parity.
Editing heap-stored function pointers after cast-mediated opaque escapes will reveal missed caller invalidations absent when edits precede escapes.
Model opaque returns with escaped-object closure and an external-unknown heap node; invalidate dependent SCCs when that closure changes.
How can opaque-call returns include newly escaped heap objects without leaving cached caller summaries stale?
Implement versioned opaque-return escape closure with caller invalidation; test staged cast escapes and heap function-pointer retargeting against semantic/full-recompute oracles.
Staged cast/indirect-call edits exposed two pre-fix may-alias omissions shared with full recomputation; 0/500 post-escape heap-pointer retargets missed caller invalidation.
Compare 1,000 before- versus after-escape heap function-pointer retargets; trace closure versions and caller invalidations against full recomputation.
NestedReturn-1000 added cast-mediated nested opaque returns absent from n26: caller invalidation missed 2/500 post-escape retargets, 0/500 pre-escape.
How should escaped-object closure track cast-mediated nested opaque returns that expose heap-stored function pointers?
Propagating nested opaque-return closure versions through cast provenance into heap-slot call-target dependencies will invalidate the two missed callers.
Use n26 and n28 failure traces to wire nested-return closure versions into heap-slot dependencies; rerun NestedReturn-1000 against full recomputation.
NestedReturn-1000: missed post-escape invalidations fell from 2/500 to 0/500; incremental and full aliases matched on all edits.
Adopt opaque-return escaped-object closure and nested heap-slot dependencies; n26 exposed omissions, n28 exposed invalidations, and n32 eliminated invalidations.
Replace coarse caller-SCC invalidation with versioned delta propagation over escaped-object closures, using wildcard heap slots for provenance-losing casts.
Extend adopted escaped-object closure with wildcard cast slots, propagate versioned SCC deltas, then benchmark semantic-oracle soundness, parity, and latency.
Extend IRSemantics-40 oracle suite with provenance-losing casts and nested opaque returns; verify closure and wildcard-slot may-alias rules.
IRSemantics-64 replaces the IRSemantics-40 oracle with 24 nested-return and provenance-losing-cast cases and explicit wildcard-slot may-alias expectations.
Run both oracle suites against incremental and full analysis; report soundness gaps separately from incremental/full alias discrepancies.
IRSemantics-64 found 4 wildcard-slot soundness gaps shared by incremental/full analysis; IRSemantics-40 showed zero incremental/full discrepancies.
Fix four IRSemantics-64 wildcard-slot gaps with conservative cast propagation; implement versioned SCC deltas and benchmark alias parity and latency.
IRSemantics-64 v2 strengthens four wildcard-slot expectations; the analyzer now propagates cast-lost heap slots and versioned SCC deltas.
Rerun IRSemantics-64 v2 and the original oracle after the four-gap fix; measure may-alias omissions and incremental/full parity.
IRSemantics-64 v2: wildcard-slot may-alias omissions fell from 4 to 0; incremental/full discrepancies remained 0 across 64 cases.
Keep conservative wildcard-slot propagation: it eliminates the four documented soundness gaps while retaining zero incremental/full discrepancies.
Can versioned closure deltas preserve ≥50% median latency reduction when wildcard heap slots expand indirect-call targets?
Deduplicating wildcard-slot delta subscriptions per caller SCC should preserve oracle parity and keep median edit latency below half full recomputation.
Deduplicate wildcard-slot subscriptions per caller SCC; run WildSlot-1000 edits, checking oracle parity and median latency against full recomputation.
WildSlot-1000: 0 oracle or full-recompute discrepancies; median edit latency 48 ms versus 112 ms full, a 57% reduction.
Use generation-stamped dependency snapshots and SCC-local rebuilds for deleted call targets and shrinking summaries, avoiding stale alias edges.
Retain sound wildcard propagation and deduplicated subscriptions; snapshot generations, rebuild deletion-affected SCCs, verify parity and ≥50% latency reduction.
Implement generation-stamped dependency snapshots atop versioned SCC deltas; rebuild affected SCCs when call targets or summaries shrink.
Generation-snapshot rebuild module records removed call-target and summary edges, then reconstructs only dependency-reachable SCCs from current IR.
Run ShrinkSCC-1000 call-target deletions and summary contractions; compare aliases and median latency against full recomputation and WildSlot-1000 baseline.
ShrinkSCC-1000: 0/1,000 alias mismatches after deletions; median edit latency 51 ms versus 112 ms full, a 54% reduction.
Adopt snapshot rebuilds with global-escape watchers, opaque-return closure, and wildcard slots: ShrinkSCC-1000 shows parity and 54% lower latency.
